Trace how a browser request for a user's profile image (avatar) is served in this Go server. I need to find:

1. The HTTP/gRPC handler that serves user profile images/avatars

Look for routes related to "avatar", "profile image", "user image", "GetUserAvatar", or similar. Check the router setup files, the user service, and any dedicated avatar/image serving endpoints. Search breadth: very thorough.

37		httpServer *http.Server
38		sseHub     *apiv1.SSEHub
39	
40		backgroundRunnerCancels []context.CancelFunc
41		backgroundRunnerWG      sync.WaitGroup
42	}

44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})
70	
71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
83	
84		// Create and register RSS routes (needs markdown service from apiV1Service).
85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}
91	
92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil
99	}

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}
133	
134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")
151	}
152	
153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}
175	
176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {
179				cancelFunc()
180			}
181		}
182	}
183	
184	func (s *Server) waitBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
185		done := make(chan struct{})
186		go func() {
187			s.backgroundRunnerWG.Wait()
188			close(done)
189		}()
190	
191		select {
192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():
194			select {
195			case <-done:
196				return
197			default:
198			}
199			slog.Error("failed to stop background runners", slog.String("error", ctx.Err().Error()))
200		}
201	}
202	
203	func (s *Server) closeLongLivedConnections() {
204		// Long-lived SSE requests do not finish on their own during http.Server.Shutdown.
205		if s.sseHub != nil {
206			s.sseHub.Close()
207		}
208	}
209	
210	func (s *Server) shutdownHTTPServer(ctx context.Context) {
211		if s.httpServer == nil {
212			return
213		}
214		if err := s.httpServer.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
215			slog.Error("failed to shutdown server", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
216			if closeErr := s.httpServer.Close(); closeErr != nil && closeErr != http.ErrServerClosed {
217				slog.Error("failed to close server", slog.String("error", closeErr.Error()))
218			}
219		}
220	}
221	
222	func (s *Server) getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx context.Context) (*storepb.InstanceBasicSetting, error) {
223		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
224		if err != nil {
225			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
226		}
227		modified := false
228		if instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey == "" {
229			instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey = uuid.NewString()
230			modified = true
231		}
232		if modified {
233			instanceSetting, err := s.Store.UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx, &storepb.InstanceSetting{
234				Key:   storepb.InstanceSettingKey_BASIC,
235				Value: &storepb.InstanceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: instanceBasicSetting},
236			})
237			if err != nil {
238				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert instance setting")
239			}
240			instanceBasicSetting = instanceSetting.GetBasicSetting()
241		}
242		return instanceBasicSetting, nil
243	}

52		if !filepath.IsAbs(dataDir) {
53			// Use current working directory, not the binary's directory
54			// This ensures we use the actual working directory where the process runs
55			absDir, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
56			if err != nil {
57				return "", err
58			}
59			dataDir = absDir
60		}

62		// Trim trailing \ or / in case user supplies
63		dataDir = strings.TrimRight(dataDir, "\\/")
64		if _, err := os.Stat(dataDir); err != nil {
65			return "", errors.Wrapf(err, "unable to access data folder %s", dataDir)

97			if err := os.MkdirAll(p.Data, 0770); err != nil {
98				slog.Error("failed to create data directory", slog.String("data", p.Data), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
99				return err

Now I have a complete picture. Let me compile the full trace.

---

Here is the complete trace of how a browser request for a user's profile image (avatar) is served in this Go server. There are **two distinct paths** through which a browser ends up fetching an avatar image.

## Path 1: The Primary Avatar Image Serving Route (HTTP/Echo)

This is the route that actually serves the raw image bytes to the browser.

### Route Registration

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/server.go` (lines 81-82)
```go
fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
```

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 121-125)
The `RegisterRoutes` method registers the Echo HTTP route:
```go
func (s *FileServerService) RegisterRoutes(echoServer *echo.Echo) {
    fileGroup := echoServer.Group("/file")
    fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)
}
```

The browser URL pattern is: `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar`

### Handler: `serveUserAvatar` (the entry point)

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 167-209)

The call chain from this handler:

**Hop 1 -- Authentication check (private instances only):**
- `serveUserAvatar` calls `s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()` (line 173)
  - **File:** `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go` (line 46-48) -- checks if `InstanceURL` is set
- If the instance is private (no InstanceURL), calls `s.getCurrentUser(ctx, c)` (line 174)
  - **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 708-712) -- delegates to `s.authenticator.AuthenticateToUser(ctx, authHeader, cookieHeader)`
    - **File:** `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` (lines 190-208) -- tries Bearer token (access token v2 or PAT), then falls back to refresh token cookie
      - `ExtractBearerToken()` -- **File:** `/bench/repo/server/auth/extract.go` (lines 11-20)
      - `resolveBearer()` -- **File:** `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` (lines 149-175) -- calls `a.store.GetUser()` to resolve the token's user
      - `ExtractRefreshTokenFromCookie()` / `AuthenticateByRefreshToken()` as fallback

**Hop 2 -- Look up the user by username:**
- `serveUserAvatar` calls `s.getUserByUsername(ctx, identifier)` (line 185)
  - **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 715-717)
    ```go
    func (s *FileServerService) getUserByUsername(ctx context.Context, identifier string) (*store.User, error) {
        return s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})
    }
    ```
  - This calls **`store.Store.GetUser()`** -- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (lines 148-169)
    - First checks the in-memory `userCache` (keyed by user ID) -- but since we're querying by username, the cache is not checked on this path
    - Calls `s.ListUsers(ctx, find)` -- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (lines 136-146)
      - Calls `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)` -- this is the **Driver interface** method (**File:** `/bench/repo/store/driver.go`, line 47)
      - The concrete implementation depends on the database driver:
        - **SQLite:** `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go` (lines 88-205) -- builds SQL `SELECT id, username, role, email, nickname, password_hash, avatar_url, description, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status FROM user WHERE username = ?`
        - **PostgreSQL:** `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go`
        - **MySQL:** `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go`
      - The `avatar_url` column is scanned directly into `user.AvatarURL` (e.g., SQLite line 189)
    - Returns the first result; populates the user cache

**Hop 3 -- Check avatar existence (line 192):**
- If `user.AvatarURL == ""`, returns 404 "avatar not found"

**Hop 4 -- Parse the data URI:**
- `serveUserAvatar` calls `s.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` (line 196)
  - **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 737-750)
  - Uses `dataURIRegex` (line 98) to extract MIME type and base64 payload from the data URI format `data:image/png;base64,...`
  - Decodes the base64 data into raw bytes

**Hop 5 -- MIME type validation (line 201):**
- Checks against `avatarAllowedTypes` map (lines 75-83): png, jpeg, jpg, gif, webp, heic, heif

**Hop 6 -- Response:**
- Sets security headers via `setSecurityHeaders(c)` (line 205)
- Sets `Content-Type` to the image MIME type and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`
- Returns the decoded image bytes via `c.Blob(http.StatusOK, imageType, imageData)` (line 209)

## Path 2: The gRPC/API Path (How the Avatar URL Gets Into the API Response)

When a browser loads a user profile via the gRPC-Gateway API (e.g., `GetUser`, `ListUsers`, `BatchGetUsers`), the API response contains an `avatar_url` field. The converter rewrites base64 data URIs into HTTP file-server URLs.

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (lines 16-42)

The function `convertUserFromStore()` performs this logic:
```go
if user.AvatarURL != "" {
    _, _, err := extractImageInfo(user.AvatarURL)
    if err == nil {
        // It's a base64 data URI -- replace with file-server URL
        userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name)
    } else {
        // It's an external URL -- keep as-is
        userpb.AvatarUrl = user.AvatarURL
    }
}
```

Where `userpb.Name` is `"users/{username}"` (built by `BuildUserName` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_resource_name.go`, line 13), so the resulting URL is `/file/users/{username}/avatar` -- which routes back to Path 1 above.

## Path 3: How Avatars Are Stored (Upload Path)

Avatars are set via the `UpdateUser` gRPC call with `"avatar_url"` in the update mask.

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` (lines 335-354)
- Validates the data URI MIME type against allowed types (png, jpeg, jpg, gif, webp)
- Sets `update.AvatarURL = &request.User.AvatarUrl`
- Calls `s.Store.UpdateUser(ctx, update)` (line 385)
  - **File:** `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (lines 126-134) -- delegates to `s.driver.UpdateUser()` and updates the cache
  - **SQLite:** `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go` (lines 48-49) -- `SET avatar_url = ?`

## ACL Note

The ACL config at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` (line 25) lists `"/memos.api.v1.UserService/GetUserAvatar"` as a public method, but **no such gRPC RPC exists** in the proto definition at `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto`. This appears to be a stale/phantom entry. The actual avatar serving is done entirely through the Echo HTTP file server route, not gRPC.

## Complete Call Chain Summary (Image Serving)

```
Browser GET /file/users/{username}/avatar
  |
  v
Echo router --> FileServerService.serveUserAvatar()           [fileserver.go:168]
  |
  |--> Profile.AllowAnonymous()                               [profile.go:46]
  |     (if private instance)
  |     |--> FileServerService.getCurrentUser()               [fileserver.go:708]
  |           |--> Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser()          [authenticator.go:190]
  |                 |--> resolveBearer() -> store.GetUser()    [authenticator.go:149]
  |                 |--> AuthenticateByRefreshToken()          [authenticator.go:61]
  |
  |--> FileServerService.getUserByUsername()                   [fileserver.go:715]
  |     |--> store.Store.GetUser()                            [store/user.go:148]
  |           |--> store.Store.ListUsers()                    [store/user.go:136]
  |                 |--> Driver.ListUsers()                   [store/driver.go:47]
  |                       |--> sqlite.DB.ListUsers()          [db/sqlite/user.go:88]
  |                             (SQL: SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?)
  |
  |--> FileServerService.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)         [fileserver.go:737]
  |     (regex parse data:image/png;base64,... -> type + bytes)
  |
  |--> avatarAllowedTypes[imageType] check                    [fileserver.go:201]
  |
  |--> setSecurityHeaders()                                   [fileserver.go:758]
  |--> c.Blob(200, imageType, imageData)                      [fileserver.go:209]
```
